title: Uttara-vibhaga. Lahari 14. The Receiving by Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu, in a Dream, of the Command of Sri Sri Bhagavan to Depart to Krishna's Abode, at Bhograi
html:
A song in glory of Shyamananda; Rasika visits Kendubilva, the place of Jayadeva, Vishnupur and Ambuya, goes round the holy places on both banks of the Ganga and every year goes to Nilachala for the Ratha-yatra; in every land he spreads the talk of Krishna, service to the guru, Krishna, the sadhus and the brahmanas, and kirtan, and on the road Sri Chaitanya travelled he performs worship; his daily and nightly routine is described by dandas; every year he celebrates twelve festivals, and all Utkala takes refuge in Krishna; one day in seclusion Rasika reflects that Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates have disappeared, and Shyamananda and the mahantas too have departed, and resolves to return to his own abode, to Krishna in Vrindavana; he reveals this to those close to him and tells two of them — Gopijanavallabha and Tulasi — that at Bhograi after sankirtana, as he was pondering a book with closed eyes, the youthful Shyama with a flute appeared to him and bade him depart, and when he hesitated, angrily repeated the command three times; they fall to the ground, and Rasika, embracing them, says that he will always remain with them

The fourteenth lahari.

Raga Karuna-shri.1
Ghosha: "It remains to proclaim the qualities of the moon Gauranga."

1Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the ocean of mercy,
whose own servant from birth is the son of Achyuta!2

2At that time Rasikendra [passed] through Kendubilva;
seeing the place of Jayadeva, he became absorbed in bhava.

3Viewing Vishnupur with delight for some days,
Rasika came to Ambuya to bathe in the Ganga.3

4He wanders, visiting the holy places on both banks of the Ganga;
he sees Sri Chaitanya-chand [and] Nityananda-raya.

5All the holy places of the mahantas that were on both banks
Rasika-shekhara viewed with joy in his heart.4

6From there Rasikendra came in haste [to Nilachala];
every year he sees Jagannatha on the chariot.

7Every year, going to the abode of Nilachala,
the son of Achyuta performs many pastimes.

8Every year he made festival pilgrimages;
for twelve months [of the year] he always wanders, renowned in the world.5

9In every land he joyfully spread the talk of Krishna,
service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus, the "Bhagavata" [and] the "Gita."

10Service to the brahmanas, service to the sadhus, the spreading of kirtan —
in every land he widely spread this dharma.

11Love for Krishna, the sixty-four [limbs] of bhakti and the rest
Rasika-Murari makes manifest in every land.6

12Not for one day does he know anything other than Krishna;
night and day Rasika always meditates on Krishna.

13In the houses of all [his] disciples, [their] disciples' disciples [and] brothers
Rasikendra always dances in sankirtana.7

14[On the road] by which Sri Chaitanya-chandra went to Jagannatha and back —
on that road Rasikendra performs worship in many ways.8

15Somewhere he worships, somewhere he rolls [on the ground],
somewhere in sankirtana tears flow.9

16Service to Krishna, worship of Krishna, sankirtana of Krishna;
ceaselessly he listens to talks about Krishna.

17In the morning — darshan of the mangala-arati;
for two dandas Prabhu meets with the Vaishnavas.10

18Then for four dandas he reads stotras, [scriptures] and so on;
bathing, worship of the Deity, remembrance and so on — four dandas.

19Then two dandas — meditation in great absorption in bhava;
then four dandas — immersed in the rasa of the Bhagavata.

20Then for two dandas he has the sadhus fed;
then for six dandas he hears the Puranas.

21Then six dandas — with his circle, in the rasa of song:
Jayadeva's Gita-govinda and other works, in endless variety.11

22Thus he spends the day in the rasa of Krishna;
as evening comes, Prabhu beholds the arati.

23For two dandas of the night he converses with the Vaishnavas;
eight dandas of the night — the delight of kirtan.

24Then six dandas of the night — a gathering for music:
various instruments, various songs, wondrous tales.

25From various lands skilled people come and stay [with him];
joyfully Prabhu listens to the singing of all.12

26Two dandas at night — the feeding of the sadhus;
together with the sadhus he joyfully eats.

27Then for six dandas of the night he reads the Bhagavata,
sitting on his asana in seclusion, entirely alone.

28Then for six dandas of the night he chants the Hari-nama;
resting in yoga-nidra, he ever meditates on Krishna.13

29Day and night, in every moment when there is leisure —
ceaselessly the Hari-nama, with eyes full of tears.

30Always he chants the Hari-nama, holding the knots in his hand;
on roads and at landings he wanders, chanting the Hari-nama.14

31Day and night there is no rest [for him], not for a moment;
apart from Krishna, Rasika knows nothing.

32Ceaselessly his mind is intoxicated with the rasa of sankirtana;
ceaselessly he explains to all the truth about Krishna.

33Ceaselessly he travels for the sake of living beings;
freeing all from ignorance, he bestowed prema [on them].

34He destroyed the evil desires of all people;
all people became intoxicated with prema-bhakti for Krishna.

35To all the wicked, as many as there were in the whole world,
he proclaimed prema-bhakti in their hearts.

36The moon of Rasikendras, whose vow is to destroy adharma,
establishes dharma with joy in his heart,

37as Krishna, descending age after age,
establishes the sadhus, destroying the wicked.15

38Such a mahashaya, the crown jewel of Rasikendras,
destroying their sins, made everyone a sadhu.16

39Many lilas he performed in the world;
he distributed love for Krishna in every single home.

40The mantra of Krishna, the tantra of Krishna, initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna and so on, the essence [and] meaning of the Vedas and shastras that are well known —

41with the consent of all the shastras, drawing out [their] essence,
he preached exclusive bhakti for Krishna.

42All the bhakti that the scriptures have described for the good of living beings —
all that bhakti the son of Achyuta revealed.17

43Nothing more remained [to be done] in accomplishing bhakti;
the whole world became filled with love for Krishna.

44The forest land of Utkala overflowed [with prema];
all understood: all [else] is false, Krishna is the true Lord.

45Twelve festivals every year
Rasika-shekhara celebrated in great bliss.18

46All the kings and subjects there are in Orissa —
disciples, disciples of disciples [and] servants [of his] in every home.

47Day and night they hold festivals everywhere;
with all their might they serve guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus.

48Nothing remained with which to gladden [the world further]:
all in the land of Utkala had taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna].19

49One day Rasika-mahashaya, sitting in seclusion,
reflected in his heart:

50by the word of all the sadhus [he] came to Bharata;
dispelling ignorance, [he] made all people sadhus.20

51[He] sees: the whole world has taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna];
in the hearts of children, the old [and] the young — the preaching [of] Krishna.21

52Women, men, and even the low-born [and] the Pukkashas,
Hunas, Pulindas and others, mlecchas, yavanas, rakshasas,

53brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, shudras and others, as many [as there are] —
all, having taken exclusive shelter, are intoxicated with love for Krishna.22

54Apart from the jubilant clamour [of the name] of Krishna, nothing else is heard;
the whole world floats in the bliss of love for Krishna.

55"I do not know what the terrible [age of] Kali will do at some time;
apart from this happiness, I see nothing else with my eyes."23

56Service to the guru, Krishna [and] the sadhus, festivals [and] processions
for sixty-two years [he] performed — renowned in the world.

57Having come to earth, [he] took the shelter of Krishna;
in the bliss of love for Krishna he passed the time.24

58"Chaitanya Gosani, Nityananda, Advaita and others — all have disappeared, [and with Them] Their associates, intimates, those who took refuge [in Them] and others.25

59Now [both] Shyamananda Prabhu [and] the host of mahantas —
before my eyes they have all departed.

60Now, I understand, the terrible [age of] Kali will manifest:
all the sadhus have left [their] pastimes on earth.26

61I too shall go to my own place;
I shall go [and] see with my eyes Sri Nandanandana —

62the Lord of Sri Radhika's life, Bhagavan Himself;
Krishna together with the maidens of Vraja I shall see with my eyes:

63in Vrindavana, on the bank of the Yamuna, in the forest groves,
at the foot of the wish-fulfilling tree, Krishna on a throne of jewels —

64bent in three places, graceful, Shyama, all-enchanting,
the youthful adolescent — between Radha and Chandravali.

65Throng after throng the maidens of Vraja serve [Him] always;
the land [there] is chintamani, [that] abode cannot be described.27

66In such an abode I shall enjoy pastimes with Krishna;
I shall leave this body — this earthly dwelling — this very day."28

67Thus in seclusion [he] ponders all this in his mind;
the son of Achyuta disclosed [it] to those close to him.29

68Hearing this, all [felt as if] struck on the head by a thunderbolt;
rolling on the ground, they weep before Prabhu.30

69Prabhu says: "Gopijanavallabha [and] Tulasi!
More than life I love you all.31

70Birth after birth you all are dear to me;
many pastimes [you have] performed [with me] in the land of Utkala.

71Whatever plans there were in my mind —
without your company I carry [them] out no longer.32

72Therefore I tell one thing to you two:
today, sitting in seclusion, I was pondering a book.

73After the sankirtana, in that place, at Bhograi,
pondering the book, [I] was sitting with closed eyes.33

74A form [the colour] of a fresh cloud, a youthful adolescent,
in His hand an enchanting flute, beautiful to behold.

75Coming before me, He spoke a word:
'The command [is given]: Rasikendra, depart!'34

76Absorbed in the taste of pondering the book, I delayed;
then, growing angry, He spoke a word:

77'You do not heed the command, Rasika-mahashaya!
To Krishna's abode, to your own place, set out!'35

78Commanding thus, He vanished,
and I, as if in a dream-trance, seemed to part with life.

79This command was given to me at the end of the night:
again and again, three times He commanded insistently."36

80Hearing these words, both fell to the ground;
smiling, the jewel of Rasikendras speaks the truth [to them].

81Embracing [them], Prabhu says: "Listen, you two:
I am always with you."37

82Nothing can be described of Rasika's life:
having descended, he purified the earth.

83He delivered the three worlds by the mercy of [his] feet —
Rasikendra-raya, whose vow is to be a sheltering enclosure.38

84[His] pastimes are a boundless ocean, they cannot be described;
in brief I have described [them] by the mercy of his feet.

85Listen to the "Rasika-mangala," all you sadhus:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of loving devotion to Krishna.39

86Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

Thus in the Uttara-vibhaga of the "Sri Rasika-mangala" ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Receiving by Sri Sri Rasikananda Prabhu, in a Dream, of the Command of Sri Sri Bhagavan to Depart to Krishna's Abode, at Bhograi."40

Notes

  1. The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Raga Karuna-shri (karuṇāśrī; Purva, lahari 1, note 8; Dakshina, lahari 1, note 1); the ghosha is the same as in Purva, lahari 2 (note 1), and its translation is repeated: gaurāṅga-cā̃dera guṇa rahilā ghoṣite. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-উত্তর-বিভাগে ভোগরাইতে কৃষ্ণধামে গমনে শ্রীশ্রীরসিকানন্দ প্রভু প্রতি স্বপ্নাবেশে শ্রীশ্রীভগবদাদেশ-প্রাপ্তি-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (bhogarāite kṛṣṇadhāme gamane śrīśrīrasikānanda prabhu prati sbapnābeśe śrīśrībhagabadādeśa-prāpti); "to depart to Krishna's abode" — kṛṣṇadhāme gamane, literally "concerning going to Krishna's abode"; "in a dream" — sbapnābeśe, "in a dream vision"; "at Bhograi" — apparently where Rasika received the command. Bhograi — a locality in the present Balasore district (Orissa), near the mouth of the Suvarnarekha. The summary line covers the whole lahari.
  2. "The son of Achyuta" (1) — acyuta-kuṅara (kũar, "prince, son"), Rasika. "Own servant from birth" — nija bhṛtya janma; it can also be understood as "whose own servant is the one born [as] the son of Achyuta."
  3. Kendubilva (kendubilba, 2) — Kenduli on the Ajay river (Birbhum district), the birthplace of Jayadeva, the author of the "Gita-govinda." "Became absorbed in bhava" — bhābābeśa haiẏā. Vishnupur (3) — Bishnupur (Bankura district), the capital of Mallabhum, the kingdom of Vira Hambira, a disciple of Shrinivasa Acharya. "With delight" — kautuke. Ambuya (āmbuẏā) — Ambika (Kalna) and its surroundings (Purva, lahari 2, note 8). "Came" — bije kailā.
  4. "Holy places" (4, 5) — pāṭa (shripat): places connected with Mahaprabhu's associates and their descendants. "He sees Sri Chaitanya-chand [and] Nityananda-raya" — apparently the darshan of the Deities of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda (cf. Ambika — Purva, lahari 2, note 8). The mahantas (5) — Pashchima, lahari 7, note 37.
  5. "Came in haste" (6) — āilā tbarite: apparently to Nilachala (Puri; 7). "On the chariot" — at the Ratha-yatra (lahari 10). "Festival pilgrimages" (8) — mahotsaba-yātrā. "Renowned in the world" — jagata-bikhyātā: it may also refer to the festivals ("renowned in the world").
  6. "Joyfully spread" (9) — pramoda karila. The "Bhagavata" [and] the "Gita" — the "Srimad-Bhagavatam" and the "Bhagavad-gita" (their reading and exposition). "The sixty-four [limbs] of bhakti" (11) — catuḥṣaṣṭi bhakti: the 64 limbs (angas) of sadhana-bhakti (Dakshina, lahari 1, note 25).
  7. "Not for one day" (12) — ekadina … nāhi. "Disciples' disciples" (13) — anuśiṣya. "Brothers" — bhāi: brothers in faith or brothers by birth. "In the houses" — mandire.
  8. jagannātha gatāgate śrīcaitanya-candra / bahurūpe se pathe pūjena rasikendra: understood to mean that on the road by which Sri Chaitanya went to Puri to Jagannatha and back (through Remuna, Jajpur and other places; CC, Madhya 5, 16), Rasika performs worship in many ways — apparently at the places of Mahaprabhu's pastimes. It can also be understood as "on that road Rasikendra worships Sri Chaitanya-chandra in many ways."
  9. "Rolls [on the ground]" — gaṛi bule. "Tears flow" — bahe aśrujale.
  10. 17–28 give Rasika's daily and nightly routine. A danda (daṇḍa) is 24 minutes, 1/60 of a day and night. By day: 2 (17) + 4 + 4 (18) + 2 + 4 (19) + 2 + 6 (20) + 6 (21) = 30 dandas; by night: 2 + 8 (23) + 6 (24) + 2 (26) + 6 (27) + 6 (28) = 30 dandas; together exactly 60 dandas, a full day and night. "Darshan of the mangala-arati" (17) — maṅgala-ārati daraśana: the morning arati to the Deity. "Meets with the Vaishnavas" — baiṣṇaba-milana.
  11. "Stotras, [scriptures] and so on" (18) — staba pāṭha-ādi, lit. "stotras, reading and so on." "Worship of the Deity" — debārccanā. "Remembrance" — smaraṇa: remembrance of Krishna's lilas. "In great absorption in bhava" (19) — mahā-bhābābeśe. "Has the sadhus fed" (20) — sādhu karāẏa bhojana. "With his circle" (21) — goṣṭhī. "Jayadeva's Gita-govinda and other works" — jaẏadeba ādi grantha, lit. "Jayadeva and other books": the songs of the Gita-govinda. "In endless variety" — aśeṣa biśeṣe.
  12. "Spends" (22) — gũẏāi. "As evening comes" — sandhyā parabeśe: the evening arati. "Converses with the Vaishnavas" (23) — baiṣṇaba-sambhāṣa. "The delight of kirtan" — kīrttana-bilāsa. "A gathering for music" (24) — saṅgīta-milana. "Wondrous tales" — adbhuta kathana. "Skilled people" (25) — guṇī jana: musicians and singers.
  13. "Joyfully" (26) — kutuhale. "In seclusion" (27) — nigame (Purva, lahari 16, note 21); likewise in 49. "Entirely alone" — ekeśbara mātra. "Resting in yoga-nidra" (28) — yoganidrā abalambe: the routine leaves no time for ordinary sleep; the author apparently means that Rasika's sleep is meditation on Krishna.
  14. "Holding the knots in his hand" (30) — granthi dhari' kare: apparently counting the names on a cord with knots (granthi, "knot"). "On roads and at landings" — pathe ghāṭe: everywhere.
  15. "The truth about Krishna" (32) — kṛṣṇatattba. "Freeing all from ignorance" (33) — abidyā chāṛiẏā sabā, lit. "making all give up ignorance (avidya)." "Evil desires" (34) — durbbāsanā. "In their hearts" (35) — sabā hṛde, "in the hearts of all". "Whose vow is to destroy adharma" (36) — adharmmadhbaṃsana-bānā; bānā — "vow, sign" (Dakshina, lahari 15, note 26). 36–37 echo Bhagavad-gita 4.7–8 (paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām / dharma-saṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge). The comparison of Rasika with the descending Krishna is the author's enthusiastic praise (on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11); and Rasika's "destruction of the wicked" is their transformation: the wicked become sadhus (35, 38); cf. the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai by Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda (CB, Madhya 13).
  16. "Mahashaya" — mahāśaẏa. "The crown jewel of Rasikendras" — rasikendracūṛāmaṇi.
  17. "The essence [and] meaning of the Vedas and shastras that are well known" (40) — bedaśāstra-tattba artha ye āche prasiddhi. "With the consent of all the shastras" (41) — sarbbaśāstra sanmati; "drawing out the essence" — sāroddhāra. "Exclusive bhakti" — ananya bhakti. "For the good of living beings" (42) — prāṇihite.
  18. "Overflowed [with prema]" (44) — ḍhalaḍhala hailā, lit. "swayed, brimmed over." "The forest land of Utkala" — utkala banabhūmi. "Twelve festivals" (45) — duẏādaśa mahotsaba: twelve festivals or a twelve-day festival.
  19. "In Orissa" (46) — uṛiṣyā bhitare. "Disciples of disciples" — anuśiṣya. "With all their might" (47) — prāṇapaṇe. "Nothing remained with which to gladden [the world further]" (48) — abaśeṣa nāhi kichu pramoda karite: pramoda — "joy, rejoicing" (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 26; cf. 9 and note 6: pramoda karila, "joyfully spread"); the sense is apparently that nothing and nowhere remained to which [bhakti] could still be joyfully spread (cf. 43). "Had taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna]" — ananya-śaraṇa.
  20. With 49 begin Rasika's reflections: the world is full of love for Krishna, the Lord's associates and Shyamananda have already departed — it is time for him, too, to go to his own abode. 50 is in the third person (āilā, kailā), so no quotation marks are used here. "By the word of all the sadhus" — sādhu sabāra bacane: understood as "by the word (command) of all the sadhus"; it may also be read as a general statement: "a sadhu comes to Bharata — by the word of all — and, dispelling ignorance, makes everyone a sadhu," i.e. about the purpose of sadhus. Bharata — bhārata, India, the earthly world.
  21. Continuation of lahari 14. begins with the complete couplet ॥51॥; no couplet carries over from. 51 continues Rasika's reflections (49–50, note 20). "[He] sees" — dekhi', lit. "seeing." "Has taken exclusive shelter [of Krishna]" — ananyaśaraṇa (note 19). "The preaching [of] Krishna" — kṛṣṇa paracāra.
  22. 52–53 echo Bhagavatam 2.4.18 (kirāta-hūṇāndhra-pulinda-pukkaśā ... śudhyanti): by taking shelter of the Lord even the lowest are purified. "Women" — strīri. "The low-born" — antyaja; the Pukkashas (pukkaśa) — a tribe counted among the lowest; Hunas and Pulindas — tribes; mlecchas — barbarians outside the Vedic order; yavanas — foreigners, here apparently Muslims; "rakshasas" (rākṣasa) — apparently cruel, savage people. "Intoxicated" — matta.
  23. "The jubilant clamour [of the name] of Krishna" (54) — kṛṣṇakolāhala. "Floats" — bhāse. 55 is in the first person (nā jāni, nā dekhi): here Rasika's words to himself begin; 56–57 are again in the third person (kaila, karilā), the author's words, so the quotation marks close after 55 and open again at 58 (ibe bujhi, "now, I understand"; āmio, "I too"), running to 66. "The terrible [age of] Kali" — ghora kali. "At some time" — kakhane. "This happiness" — ei sukha: the world full of love for Krishna (51–54).
  24. "Festivals [and] processions" (56) — mahotsaba-yātrā. "Sixty-two years" — bāṣaṭṭi batsara: the length of Rasikananda's life (1590–1652); in lahari 15, 37 — "sixty-two years and four months." "Renowned in the world" — jagata bikhyātā. "Having come to earth" (57) — bhūmigata haiẏā, lit. "having fallen to the ground," i.e. from his very birth. "Passed the time" — kāla karilā haraṇa.
  25. "Have disappeared" (58) — gupta hailā: the departure of the Lord and His associates is a disappearance from the manifest lila. "Their associates, intimates, those who took refuge [in Them]" — sāṅgopāṅgāśraya: sāṅgopāṅga, lit. "with limbs and sub-limbs," i.e. with the closest associates and their followers; āśraya — those who took refuge [in Them]; the same expression is in lahari 16, 5.
  26. "The host of mahantas" (59) — mohāntera gaṇa. "Before my eyes" — dekhite dekhite, lit. "while [I] was watching," i.e. one after another and quickly. On Shyamananda's departure — Pashchima, lahari 13. "Have departed" — karilā gamana. "Pastimes on earth" (60) — pṛthibī-bilāsa.
  27. "My own place" (61) — āpanā sthāne: the eternal abode (cf. 77: nijasthāne). Nandanandana — "the son of Nanda," Krishna. "The Lord of Sri Radhika's life" (62) — śrīrādhikā-prāṇapati; "Bhagavan Himself" — sbaẏaṃ bhagabān. "The maidens of Vraja" — brajāṅganā. "On the bank of the Yamuna, in the forest groves" (63) — yamunā pulina kuñjabane. "Bent in three places" (64) — tribhaṅga. Chandravali — the leader of the group of gopis rivalling Radha; pre-eminence among the gopis belongs to Radha (cf. 62). "Throng after throng" (65) — yūtha yūtha: a yutha is a group of gopis under a leader. "The land is chintamani" — bhūmi cintāmaṇi: the land of Vrindavana is made of wish-fulfilling chintamani stones; cf. Brahma-samhita 5.56 (bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayī), which also names the wish-fulfilling trees (63).
  28. "I shall enjoy pastimes" (66) — kariba bilāsa. "I shall leave this body" — chāṛiba e deha (so in the text). "This earthly dwelling" — pṛthibīnibāsa: understood as in apposition to "body"; it can also be read "I shall leave ... my life on earth." In the Gaudiya Vaishnava understanding the departure of an associate of the Lord is not an end under the rule of karma but a passage into the eternal (unmanifest) lila. "This very day" — āji.
  29. "In seclusion" (67) — nigame (note 13). "To those close to him" — ātmagaṇe. The son of Achyuta is Rasika.
  30. "Struck on the head by a thunderbolt" (68) — muṇḍe haila bajrāghāta. "Rolling" — luṭhiẏā. "Before Prabhu" — prabhura sākṣāta.
  31. "Gopijanavallabha [and] Tulasi" (69) — gopījanaballabhatulasī, a single compound; understood as two names (cf. 72, 80, 81: "you two," "both"). Gopijanavallabha is possibly the author himself, Gopijana-vallabha Dasa, the son of Rasamaya; Tulasi is apparently Thakura Tulasi (Tulasidasa), the kirtan singer (Uttara, lahari 2, note 15; Purva, lahari 1, note 34). "More than life" — prāṇa haite.
  32. "Birth after birth" (70) — janme janme. "Many pastimes [you have] performed [with me]" — aneka karilā khelā: karilā is taken as a second-person form; it can also be read "[I] performed." "In the land of Utkala" — utkala-bhubana. "Plans" (71) — bicāra. "Without your company I carry [them] out no longer" — tomā sabā saṅga binā nā kariẏe āra: i.e. he does nothing without sharing it with them — and therefore discloses the command to them.
  33. "One thing" (72) — eka kathā. "Pondering a book" — puṃthi cintā kari: apparently a sacred book he was reading (which one is not said). "After the sankirtana" (73) — saṃkīrttana upānte. "In that place, at Bhograi" — se bhogarāi sthāne (note 1). "[I] was sitting" — baise, lit. "sits" (third person): Rasika speaks of himself as of another. "With closed eyes" — mudritanaẏane.
  34. "[The colour] of a fresh cloud" (74) — nabaghanaśyāma; "a youthful adolescent" — nabīna kiśora: Krishna (the colophon speaks of "the command of Sri Sri Bhagavan"). "Flute" — bā̃śī. "The command [is given]" (75) — ājñā hailā.
  35. "I delayed" (76) — karilũ helana, lit. "I neglected, disregarded." "You do not heed the command" (77) — ājñā nāhi māna. "Mahashaya" — mahāśaẏa. "Set out" — karaha bijaẏa: of a ceremonial departure (lahari 2, note 28).
  36. "He vanished" (78) — haila antarddhāna. "As if in a dream-trance, seemed to part with life" — yena sbapnābeśe tejinu parāṇa: i.e. from the shock he as it were lost consciousness; hence the colophon's "in a dream" (sbapnābeśe). "At the end of the night" (79) — niśi śeṣe: apparently the vision came in the night after the sankirtana (72–73); "today" (72) — on the same day. "Three times He commanded" — tina ājñā karila, lit. "gave three commands"; "insistently" — biśeṣe.
  37. "Both" (80) — dõhā. "Smiling" — hāsiẏā. "The truth" — tattba. "The jewel of Rasikendras" — rasikendramaṇi. "Embracing [them]" (81) — kole kari', "taking into his arms." "Always" — anukṣaṇa, "every moment": a promise to remain with those close to him even after his departure.
  38. From 82 — the author's words. "Of Rasika's life" — rasika-caritra. "Having descended" — abatīrṇa haiẏā: the author's enthusiastic praise (on the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11; cf. note 15). "He delivered the three worlds" (83) — uddhārila tina loka. "Whose vow is to be a sheltering enclosure" — śaraṇapañjarabānā: śaraṇa-pañjara — "a cage (enclosure) of refuge," i.e. a sure protection for those who take shelter; bānā — "vow, sign" (note 15). Raya — rāẏa, an honorific, "lord."
  39. "A boundless ocean" (84) — apāra samudra. "In brief" — saṃkṣepe. "By the mercy of his feet" — tā̃ra caraṇakṛpāẏa. "Without delay" (85) — abilambe. "The treasure of loving devotion to Krishna" — kṛṣṇapremabhaktidhana.
  40. The author's signature (86) and the colophon are; the title is as in note 1 (sbapnābeśe, "in a dream"). Below is a rule.
